topic: Phenotype- / Cohort-linked Spatial Feature and Niche Analysis
fields: Do Not Start With This When

rows.Main Input: multi-sample ST or spatial single-cell datasets + coordinates and optional image-like or cell-type channels
rows.Main Use in This Topic: learning cross-sample tissue motif representations for cohort- or condition-associated spatial features
rows.Main Output: self-supervised tissue representations, motif enrichment, and motif-associated differential features
rows.Key Difference: Learns tissue motif representations for cross-sample comparison rather than using a transparent DE model, bulk phenotype transfer, multi-slice supervised niche model, or tissue-cellular-neighborhood discovery.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Cell Systems paper; official documentation and Zenodo point to the Broad Institute repository and GPU-oriented workflow. Layer 2 synthesis: retained as representation-mediated cohort motif / differential spatial transcriptomics evidence, not direct gene-level contrast testing. Code/access fields are trace metadata only and do not imply execution readiness.
rows.Best First Choice When: Consider when many samples are available and the deliverable is learned tissue motifs or cohort-associated microenvironment representations.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: Do not use when the requested deliverable is a transparent gene-level contrast test, within-sample SVG ranking, pathology-severity scoring, or cohort-linked TCN/community discovery.
rows.Main Feature or Niche Output: self-supervised tissue representations, motif enrichment, and motif-associated differential features
rows.Boundary Placement Cue: Use this topic only when motif or feature association is the deliverable; direct DE or spatial-pattern contrast belongs in Spatial Contrast Testing.
rows.Primary Validity Caveat: Self-supervised representations can encode acquisition, tissue composition, sample processing, or preprocessing structure rather than biological condition effects; motif association is not causality.

rows.Main Input: ST data + spatial features + bulk RNA-seq cohort profiles with clinical phenotype annotations
rows.Main Use in This Topic: linking spatial tumor microenvironment features to phenotype or clinical outcome signals through bulk cohorts
rows.Main Output: phenotype-associated spatial TME features, factors, and linked architectures
rows.Key Difference: Uses bulk cohort phenotypes to link ST-derived TME features to clinical outcomes, rather than directly testing condition DE inside the ST cohort alone.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Cell Genomics paper and public full text describes bulk-spatial phenotype linking. Code access remains unclear in this bounded pass because no primary repository URL was confirmed. Code/access fields are trace metadata only and do not imply execution readiness.
rows.Best First Choice When: Consider when spatial features should be associated with clinical phenotypes through a larger bulk RNA-seq cohort.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: Do not use when bulk cohort phenotype data are unavailable, when a direct ST-only contrast test is required, or when the requested output is a pathology score.
rows.Main Feature or Niche Output: phenotype-associated spatial TME features, factors, and linked architectures
rows.Boundary Placement Cue: Use this topic when the central deliverable is phenotype-associated spatial features rather than direct DE.
rows.Primary Validity Caveat: Bulk-to-spatial transfer can introduce cohort, tumor-purity, cell-composition, and phenotype-label confounding.

rows.Main Input: bulk RNA-seq expression with clinical or phenotype table plus scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics inference data
rows.Main Use in This Topic: prioritizing phenotype-associated cells, spots, and spatial niches for clinical biomarker discovery
rows.Main Output: TiRank scores, TiRank labels, and phenotype-associated spatial or cellular niches
rows.Key Difference: Transfers phenotype associations from bulk clinical cohorts into scRNA-seq or spatial spots/cells using relative-expression-ordering gene-pair features and multitask learning.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: targeted check verifies PMID 41689080, DOI 10.1186/s13073-026-01604-2, Genome Medicine 2026, public GitHub, and TiRank documentation. Layer 2 synthesis: branch placement follows phenotype-linked niche prioritization. Code access is trace metadata only and does not imply execution readiness.
rows.Best First Choice When: Consider when bulk clinical or phenotype data should guide prioritization of phenotype-associated cells, spots, or spatial niches in scRNA-seq or ST data.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: Do not use for unsupervised niche discovery, within-sample SVG detection, direct condition-contrast DE testing, or pathology-score estimation.
rows.Phenotype / Cohort Signal: bulk clinical phenotype or outcome signal
rows.Main Feature or Niche Output: TiRank score/label and phenotype-associated niches or subpopulations
rows.Boundary Placement Cue: Use this topic because the deliverable is phenotype-associated niche prioritization, not direct DE or SVG.
rows.Primary Validity Caveat: Phenotype-label leakage, cross-modality transfer, gene coverage/dropout sensitivity, and clinical association versus causal interpretation require explicit review.

rows.Main Input: multi-slice spatial omics profiles, spatial coordinates, and optional clinical or phenotype labels
rows.Main Use in This Topic: identifying clinically or phenotypically relevant niches from integrated spatial multi-slice or multi-omics data
rows.Main Output: phenotype-linked niches, slice-level niche vectors, niche weights, predicted hazard ratios or class labels, and interpreted high-risk or phenotype-associated niches
rows.Key Difference: Uses dynamic graph integration across spatial multi-slice or multi-omics data and links learned niches to clinical or phenotype labels.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: targeted check verifies PMID 40523901, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-60575-x, Nature Communications 2025, public GitHub, and Zenodo record 15246396. Layer 2 synthesis: branch placement follows phenotype-linked niche output rather than generic integration or clustering. Code access is trace metadata only and does not imply execution readiness.
rows.Best First Choice When: Consider when multi-slice spatial omics should be integrated to identify clinically or phenotypically relevant niches and phenotype-prediction weights.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: Do not use when the task is only spatial integration, plain domain clustering, generic graph-neighborhood discovery, direct condition-contrast testing, or pathology-score estimation.
rows.Phenotype / Cohort Signal: clinical phenotype, survival, class label, or cohort signal
rows.Main Feature or Niche Output: clinically relevant niches, niche vectors, and phenotype-linked niche weights
rows.Transfer / Representation Dependence: multi-slice graph integration and supervised phenotype weighting
rows.Boundary Placement Cue: Use this topic because phenotype-linked niche interpretation is the deciding deliverable; cross-reference Integration, Domain / Clustering, and Graph / Neighborhood as upstream machinery only.
rows.Primary Validity Caveat: Supervised phenotype weighting can leak labels; cohort, platform, batch, slice, and tissue-composition confounding can shape learned niches; latent representation opacity should be preserved as a caveat.

rows.Main Input: spatial cell phenotypes or spatial expression with coordinates, neighborhood graph, and cohort/condition/phenotype labels
rows.Main Use in This Topic: identifying cohort- or phenotype-associated tissue cellular neighborhoods and community features
rows.Main Output: cohort-associated tissue cellular neighborhoods, community features, and niche summaries
rows.Key Difference: Centers supervised or condition-associated tissue cellular neighborhood discovery rather than bulk phenotype transfer, multi-slice clinical niche integration, or self-supervised tissue motif representation.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Methods CytoCommunity method identity (PMID 38191930; DOI 10.1038/s41592-023-02124-2), and the Graph / Neighborhood package records the public code trace. Layer 2 synthesis: included here as a controlled duplicate only for cohort- or phenotype-linked TCN/community feature analysis. Code access is trace metadata only and no Layer 3 runtime, callable, adapter, backend binding, or execution-environment support is implied.
rows.Best First Choice When: Consider when cohort, condition, or phenotype labels are part of the task and the requested deliverable is tissue cellular neighborhoods or community features associated with those labels.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: Do not use when the task is generic unsupervised neighborhood discovery without phenotype/cohort signal, direct contrast testing, pathology-score estimation, or causal communication inference.
rows.Main Feature or Niche Output: cohort-associated tissue cellular neighborhoods, community features, and niche summaries
rows.Boundary Placement Cue: Controlled duplicate of the Graph / Neighborhood CytoCommunity row; use only when Layer 1 has assigned the phenotype/cohort-linked Analysis Problem.
rows.Primary Validity Caveat: Supervised labels, cell phenotyping, graph construction, sampling density, cohort, batch, platform, and composition confounding can shape TCNs; associations are not causal proof.
